title: C# [GlobalClass] extending GpuParticles2D doesn't get registered in Godot's editor
body: ### Tested versions Reproducible in: - v4.6.dev1.mono.official [8d8041bd4] - v4.5.stable.mono.official [876b29033] - v4.3.stable.mono.official [77dcf97d8] Not reproducible in: - v4.1.stable.mono.official [970459615] ### System information Godot v4.5.stable.mono - Debian GNU/Linux 12 (bookworm) 12 on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Ti (nvidia) - AMD Ryzen 9 5900X 12-Core Processor (24 threads) - 31.25 GiB memory ### Issue description I have a C# script named `CustomGpuParticles2D` extending `GpuParticles2D` and I'm trying to make it appear in the "Create new node" dialog in the editor by adding the `[GlobalClass]` annotation: ```csharp using Godot; using System; [GlobalClass] public partial class CustomGpuParticles2D : GpuParticles2D { } ``` However, `CustomGpuParticles2D` doesn't appear in the "Create new node" dialog: I could only reproduce this in C# scripts. Extending `GPUParticles2D`/`HTTPRequest` from GDScript (combined with using `class_name`) works fine. It seems like this bug only affects scripts extending builtin node types, which have a different class name in C# compared to their name in the Godot editor. From testing: - Extending `Node`, `Node2D` and `Area2D` works fine - the new node types do appear in the "Create new node" dialog. - Extending `GpuParticles2D`(C#)/`GPUParticles2D`(editor) and `HttpRequest`(C#)/`HTTPRequest`(editor) triggers the bug - note the difference between the node class names exposed to C# and node class names in the Godot editor. I also found a [Reddit post](https://www.reddit.com/r/godot/comments/1gufk0u/cant_extend_gpuparticles2d/) of another user seemingly encountering the same bug. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open the attached MRP in Godot 2. Build project 3. Open the "Create new node" dialog 4. Search for "Custom" **Expected behavior**: `CustomGpuParticles2D` appears in the "Create new node" dialog. **Observed behavior**: `CustomGpuParticles2D` does not appear in the "Create new node" dialog. Note that `CustomNode2D` (extending `Node2D` - same class name in C# and GDScript) and `OtherCustomGpuParticles2D` (`GPUParticles2D` extended from GDScript) do appear in the dialog, as expected. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [gpu-particles-2d-bug-mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22695742/gpu-particles-2d-bug-mrp.zip)
